title: Speak Readings>"Or per number of minutes" text is too large
body:
doesn't match other text on that page and therefore I can't see the current setting (number of minutes).  That line and the line of text above it is out of proportion to all other text.

If you fix THIS issue, but don't fix the issue I posted about 5-6 days ago, I won't be able to use the fixed version as I won't get data on my Gear 2.

@dave1812, as I saw your message, what do you think, after your directly delete it? Please keep in mind all devs are private persons with work, family and a lot of progress beside! Surly if someone have time he will check the issue, but sometimes other issues are more important... 

Anyway some questions:
- As you say something about Gear2, I want to ask you, does Gear2 have to do something with this issue you posted here (I'm asking that because mixing informations in one issue is not a good idea).
- which phone you use, and which Rom?
- did you change display settings in the phone (dpi or font size)?
- did you use theme-apps like substratum?
- did you try to change the orientation of the phone to see the setting completely? (Workaround)

**thanks for requesting further clarification.**

I'm just an end user so I don't know what substratum is!

1. My watch is a Gear 2 which runs Tizen.  No way that I could know if the issue extends to other watches receiving Notifications.   Keep in mind, I do NOT use an app on the Gear 2.  Just Android Notifications functions to receive xdrip readings every 5 minutes.  it works great, but not for the newer builds.  I've no idea on which date, the function became broken but 7/15 version works fine.  However this Gear 2 talk has nothing to do with the issue on this thread.  I made another posting for the Gear 2 issue.
2. S7 running android 8.0.0
3. display settings are Screen Zoom=Middle of the range, as is Font Size.
4. don't use any themes
5. I can see the minutes if I rotate, so that is a "yes".

The only outsized fonts on that page seem to be the two lines that I mentioned in the OP.
ah, thanks for the explanation.  if the text size is fixed in a daily release, will anyone be updating this thread?

@jamorham & colleagues
An additional feature of this section: I use xdrip while biking. To me, is quite important to know how much it raises/decreases, and not only the label of the trend (slight up/down...). The possibility that one can select between xdrip speaking aloud the number of the delta or the text label would be a nice improvement. A toogle button in the 3 dots menu on the uppermost left will suffice. 
I don't know how to do this in the code. Anyone else see this feature as interesting for having a "normal" life?
Sorry, but I don't know how to use the "pull request" feature of this site
thanks!
this looks like something I could to to get into the xDrip code. I can confirm the symptoms on my phone, that's something. *forked*

At the moment I'm not complete clear on that. If you add android:textSize="5sp" in pref_advanced_settings.xml to all SeekBarPreference's, the size will be fine on my phone. But I'm pretty sure that this is not the usual way to set the font size in relation to the rest of all preference entrys. I would expect that Resources should be set for that, but I did not see any other font-Settings up to now... @jamorham, is there a general setting for Fontsize of the Prefs, where maybe the SeekBar should be included?

Adding a `textSize` element to the `SeekBarPreference` definition in the xml makes no difference to size on my phone (sony android 6)

I think it has to be done with a custom layout for `SeekBarPreference` which I think has a `layout` xml parameter. When I tried this recently I got a crash I couldn't determine the source of and haven't pursued it further.

Mysteriuos... Which value you given in the `SeekBarPreference` ? I was not sure that `android:textSize="5sp"` is right, but with that value it was rendered right on my Androidemulator...

Did you have your try with `Layout xml` as a patch? Then I would try to investigate that further, as I think it is better to use it in that standard approach.
